subject: The note-ban anniversary and the 'corruption ended' poster
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: a poster in a gold frame hangs on the wall. In it a white-bearded man in khaki safari clothes and a hat stands with one foot on a dark buffalo-like demon and raises two fingers in a V sign; a red sash across the demon's back reads CORRUPTION, and the hunter has driven a sword marked NOTE BAN into its back; below, in large letters: 2016. On the left an elderly leader with a white beard, glasses and a saffron vest stands laughing with his arms folded; his speech bubble reads: THANKS TO MY NOTE BAN ADVICE, CORRUPTION WAS ERADICATED! In the middle a man with a grey beard, hands folded, looks at the poster. On the right a young man in a blue shirt raises a hand towards the poster and says in disbelief: SO, THIS WAS INDEED FAKE! Behind the two leaders a large horned shadow of the demon falls on the wall. At the lower right, the cartoonist's signature: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: In the poster, the 2016 hunter crushes a demon called CORRUPTION with the sword of demonetisation, and the elderly leader beside it laughs and says his advice wiped corruption out. The young man on the right looks at the poster and says: so this was indeed fake!

Satish's ink is aimed at the date, not the argument. The same old 2016 poster hangs on the wall, repainted and rehung every anniversary, and the demon's shadow still falls behind the very leaders who claim to have killed it. Corruption was not killed; only its picture changed, and that too inside a frame.
